newsitem.title: USA: PP&L Susquehanna 2 nuke shuts as expected.
newsitem.headline: PP&L Susquehanna 2 nuke shuts as expected.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light Co (PP&L) said it shut its 1,094 megawatt (MW) Susquehanna nuclear power unit 2 on Saturday as expected for scheduled maintenance and refueling.
The outage is expected to last about six weeks while close to 40 percent of the unit's uranium fuel is replaced, PP&L said in a statement.
The outage at Susquehanna 2, located in Berwick, Pa., will mark the beginning of a 24-month refueling cycle for the unit, PP&L said. Previously, the unit was refueled every 18 months.
The adjacent 1,090 MW Susquehanna nuclear unit 1 was in startup mode as of early Monday, returning from a repair outage, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said in its daily plant status report.
The NRC said the unit was producing at one percent of capacity and was conducting restart tests as of early Monday.
Susquehanna 1 was taken off line Feb 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in the unit's main condenser. A restart was later delayed for work on a residual heat removal system.
Susquehanna 1 will move to a 24-month refueling cycle during its next refueling outage in the spring of 1998, PP&L said in the statement.
The Susquehanna units are jointly owned by PP&L and the Allegheny Electric Cooperative.
